easy_fields.name: LAMBADA (LAnguage Modeling Broadened to Account for Discourse Aspects) dataset
easy_fields.creator: Denis Paperno, Germán Kruszewski, Angeliki Lazaridou, Quan Ngoc Pham, Raffaella Bernardi, Sandro Pezzelle, Marco Baroni, Gemma Boleda, Raquel Fernández
easy_fields.citeAs: Paperno, D., Kruszewski, G., Lazaridou, A., Pham, Q. N., Bernardi, R., Pezzelle, S., Baroni, M., Boleda, G., & Fernández, R. (2016). The LAMBADA dataset: Word prediction requiring a broad discourse context. In Proceedings of the 54th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (pp. 1525-1534).
easy_fields.description: LAMBADA is a dataset designed to evaluate computational models for text understanding through a word prediction task. It consists of narrative passages where human subjects can guess the last word when exposed to the whole passage, but not when only seeing the last sentence, requiring models to track broader discourse context.

G3_collection.reasoning: The paper extensively details the data collection methodology, including the raw data source (Book Corpus), filtering steps, and the crowdsourcing process used to select passages.

G4_annotation.reasoning: Section 3.1 explicitly describes the human annotation protocol using the CrowdFlower service, including the multi-step process, criteria for inclusion, and payment for annotators.

G5_rai.reasoning: The paper discusses intended use cases, limitations of the dataset (e.g., strict matching criteria), potential biases (e.g., overrepresentation of proper nouns), and mentions filtering out potentially offensive material, though it lacks details on annotator demographics.

G6_processing.reasoning: The paper describes preprocessing steps like duplicate removal, filtering offensive content, and filtering passages based on language model predictions, as well as the division into training, development, and test sets, and a plan for future competition release.
